alive.last_commit_message:
Keep a 300k-message chat from blocking its worker's event loop (#1192)

A turn in a chat of hundreds of thousands of messages validated the whole
history in one transaction, merged and measured it, digested and grouped it
for compaction and offset-scanned every project message to validate its
sources, all on the worker's event loop: 15 s + 8.5 s stalls and minutes of
serialized transactions, so the worker lost its lease and the turn failed.
Opening the conversation's context status or exporting its transcript did
the same.

A conversation's history is now read a bounded keyset page per transaction,
with the same order, limits and cursors. CPU-bound pure steps over a long
history (the history merge, context sources, compaction preparation,
grouping, merging and digests, request size estimates and the context status
estimate) run in a worker thread above 2000 items, with identical results.
Compaction validates its sources against the session's own messages instead
of offset pages over the project, an append takes MAX(sequence) instead of
reading every message, and a large full transcript streams the same JSON a
slice at a time.
